sentences.zh: 虽然这个职位听起来并不令人兴奋，

sentences.en: Joe, but for nature.

sentences.zh: 他曾在太平洋上阻止过捕鲸船。

sentences.zh: 他曾救出过一只被困在印尼度假村的海豚。

sentences.zh: 那是《科学对决》的主持人温迪·扎克曼，

sentences.zh: 我很确定她只被捅过一次。

sentences.en: And recently, Pete's work brought him to Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 最近，皮特的工作把他带到了哥斯达黎加。

sentences.en: And that's where his luck almost ran out.
sentences.zh: 而就在那里，他的好运差点用尽了。

sentences.en: This was just before Christmas.
sentences.zh: 那是在圣诞节前夕。

sentences.en: Pete was deep in the rainforest with his team,
sentences.zh: 皮特和他的团队深入雨林，

sentences.zh: 他们正在寻找非法伐木和狩猎的证据。

sentences.en: Picture it.
sentences.zh: 想象一下那个画面。

sentences.en: It's a lush forest, thick canopy, very hilly.
sentences.zh: 那是一片郁郁葱葱的森林，树冠茂密，山峦起伏。

sentences.en: But it's up and down, up and down, up and down, really steep.
sentences.zh: 地形起伏不定，非常陡峭。

sentences.en: It's got the most ferocious ants on Earth.
sentences.zh: 那里有地球上最凶猛的蚂蚁。

sentences.en: It's got poisonous spiders.
sentences.zh: 还有毒蜘蛛。

sentences.en: They are all over the place.
sentences.zh: 到处都是。

sentences.en: A lot of the trees have very spiky trunks on them,
sentences.zh: 很多树的树干上长满了尖刺，

sentences.en: so you need to be really careful walking.
sentences.zh: 所以走路时必须非常小心。

sentences.en: That's Pete.
sentences.zh: 那是皮特。

sentences.en: And while he was walking very carefully through the rainforest,
sentences.zh: 当他小心翼翼地穿过雨林时，

sentences.en: something got him.
sentences.zh: 他被什么东西袭击了。

sentences.en: I just felt this bang in the back of my leg.
sentences.zh: 我只感觉到腿后部猛地一震。

sentences.en: And my first thought was someone had hit me.
sentences.zh: 我第一反应是有人打了我一下。

sentences.en: Like, it felt like someone had a big stick or a piece of wood
sentences.zh: 感觉就像有人拿着一根大棍子或一块木头，

sentences.en: and it whacked the back of my calf.
sentences.zh: 狠狠地抽在了我的小腿后面。

sentences.en: And then I looked down, and in horror,
sentences.zh: 然后我低头一看，惊恐地发现，

sentences.en: I see this snake sort of recoiling away from me with its sort of head.
sentences.zh: 一条蛇正从我身边缩回去，昂着头。

sentences.en: And it was sticking about two feet off the ground.
sentences.zh: 它离地大约两英尺高。

sentences.en: And as soon as I saw it, like, I knew it was a fur-de-lance.
sentences.zh: 我一看到它，就知道那是矛头蝮。

sentences.en: The fur-de-lance, or spearhead, is the most deadly snake in Central America.
sentences.zh: 矛头蝮，又称“矛头蛇”，是中美洲最致命的毒蛇。

sentences.en: Right away, Pete's colleague grabbed his cell phone.
sentences.zh: 皮特的同事立刻抓起手机。

sentences.en: He had one bar of reception and called up emergency services.
sentences.zh: 他只有一格信号，拨通了急救电话。

sentences.en: They did make it clear,
sentences.zh: 他们明确表示，

sentences.en: you need to get their guy to hospital as quickly as possible or he is going to die.
sentences.zh: 必须尽快把人送到医院，否则他会没命的。

sentences.en: Pete had maybe six hours to get to a hospital.
sentences.zh: 皮特可能只有六个小时的时间赶到医院。

sentences.en: And to get there, he had to dodge all the spikes and spiders
sentences.zh: 为了到达那里，他必须避开雨林里的所有尖刺、蜘蛛

sentences.en: and other snakes in the rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 以及其他毒蛇。

sentences.en: Pete had two options.
sentences.zh: 皮特有两个选择。

sentences.en: He could go up on the ridge of the mountain,
sentences.zh: 他可以走山脊，

sentences.en: which would use up his six hours.
sentences.zh: 那会耗尽他仅有的六小时。

sentences.en: Or he could go down through muddy creeks.
sentences.zh: 或者他可以穿过泥泞的溪流。

sentences.en: That would be harder, but also faster.
sentences.zh: 那样会更艰难，但速度也更快。

sentences.en: And he might get to the hospital in time.
sentences.zh: 他或许能及时赶到医院。

sentences.en: I remember looking at my map on my phone and thinking,
sentences.zh: 我记得看着手机上的地图心想，

sentences.en: you know, the only option here is we need to go down one of these creek beds.
sentences.zh: 你知道，唯一的选择就是我们得顺着这些河床走。

sentences.en: So I'm crawling on my arse,
sentences.zh: 所以我屁股着地爬着走，

sentences.en: crawling down these little waterfalls, escarpments, banks.
sentences.zh: 爬过这些小瀑布、陡坡和河岸。

sentences.en: But as we're going down, I'm getting weaker and weaker.
sentences.zh: 但随着我们不断下行，我感觉越来越虚弱。

sentences.en: And the strobbing now has moved all the way up to my groin area
sentences.zh: 毒素现在已经蔓延到了我的腹股沟区域，

sentences.en: and eventually gets a stage where I just want to sleep.
sentences.zh: 最终到了一个我只想睡觉的地步。

sentences.en: But I did think, I'm not going to make this.
sentences.zh: 但我确实想过，我撑不过去了。

sentences.en: My number was up.
sentences.zh: 我的大限已到。

sentences.en: After trudging his way through waterfalls and mud,
sentences.zh: 在跋涉过瀑布和泥潭后，

sentences.en: Pete arrived at the edge of the rainforest
sentences.zh: 皮特到达了雨林的边缘，

sentences.en: and onto a beach where he saw the Coast Guard.
sentences.zh: 来到海滩上，他看到了海岸警卫队。

sentences.en: They lay me down on the ground and I remember just closing my eyes
sentences.zh: 他们让我躺在地上，我记得我只是闭上眼睛，

sentences.en: and thinking, you know, just hang on a little bit more,
sentences.zh: 心想，再坚持一会儿，

sentences.en: hang on a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 再坚持一会儿。

sentences.en: Pete arrived at the hospital around three and a half hours
sentences.zh: 皮特在被咬后大约三个半小时，

sentences.en: after he was bitten.
sentences.zh: 被送到了医院。

sentences.en: His heart was racing and he passed out.
sentences.zh: 他的心跳加速，随后昏了过去。

sentences.en: When he came to,
sentences.zh: 当他醒来时，

sentences.en: he started documenting everything that was going on.
sentences.zh: 他开始记录发生的一切。

sentences.en: depending on where you are in the world.

sentences.en: Sort of give you guys an update

sentences.en: on what's happened over the last couple of days.
sentences.zh: 过去几天发生的事情。

sentences.zh: 蛇毒已经开始破坏他的肌肉和血管。

sentences.zh: 皮特的腿肿胀到了原来的两倍大。

sentences.zh: 这在蛇咬伤患者中并不罕见。

sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它不让人震惊。

sentences.zh: 噢，伙计，我记得。

sentences.zh: 我记得问过其中一位护士，

sentences.en: is this normal?
sentences.zh: 这正常吗？

sentences.zh: 啊，是的，算是吧，可能。

sentences.zh: 为了扭转局面，

sentences.zh: 是一个复杂、耗时且低效的过程，

sentences.zh: 好吧，那为什么制造抗蛇毒血清这么难？

sentences.zh: 有时两种不同的毒素可以协同工作，

sentences.zh: 但当你把它们放在一起时，

sentences.zh: 由于身体无法凝血来阻止这种内出血，

sentences.zh: 种类的蛇，比如黑曼巴蛇、蝰蛇、响尾蛇，你就不需要

sentences.en: through this whole process so many times in so many different countries.
sentences.zh: 在这么多不同的国家多次经历整个过程了。

sentences.en: Well, it sounds super easy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听起来超级简单。

sentences.en: Why don't we just do that?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不直接那样做呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's not easy and it takes a lot of time and innovative thinking and the big thing
sentences.zh: 嗯，这并不容易，需要花费大量的时间和创新思维，而最主要的问题

sentences.en: is money.
sentences.zh: 是钱。

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: And for a long time, no one was really putting a lot of money into this space.
sentences.zh: 而且很长一段时间以来，真的没有人在这个领域投入大量资金。

sentences.en: And that's for all kinds of complicated reasons.
sentences.zh: 这有各种复杂的原因。

sentences.en: But if we had to boil it down to a word, I would say that word was capitalism.
sentences.zh: 但如果非要用一个词来概括，我会说是资本主义。

sentences.en: So as we talked about, snakebites kill around 100,000 people every year.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所谈到的，蛇咬伤每年导致约10万人死亡。

sentences.en: This is a serious problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个严重的问题。

sentences.en: But most of those deaths are happening in rural areas in Africa and Asia for people who can't
sentences.zh: 但大多数死亡发生在非洲和亚洲的农村地区，那里的人们

sentences.en: afford a lot of money for medication.
sentences.zh: 负担不起昂贵的药物。

sentences.en: And drug companies haven't put a lot of funding into this to try and make things better, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上，制药公司并没有投入大量资金来尝试改善这种情况。

sentences.en: But since 2017, things have started to change.
sentences.zh: 但自2017年以来，情况开始发生变化。

sentences.en: What happened in 2017?
sentences.zh: 2017年发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the World Health Organization gave snakebites this special designation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，世界卫生组织给了蛇咬伤一个特殊的称号。

sentences.en: They listed them as the most important kind of neglected tropical disease.
sentences.zh: 他们将其列为最重要的被忽视的热带病。

sentences.en: This sounds terribly nerdy and in the weeds, but basically what it means for a disease is
sentences.zh: 这听起来非常书呆子气且深奥，但对于一种疾病来说，这意味着

sentences.en: that it's kind of like winning an Oscar.
sentences.zh: 它有点像获得了奥斯卡奖。

sentences.en: You get extra attention.
sentences.zh: 你会得到额外的关注。

sentences.en: You get extra money.
sentences.zh: 你会得到额外的资金。

sentences.en: That is basically what's happened.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是发生的事情。

sentences.en: We've seen this real change in what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了情况的真正转变。

sentences.en: You know, you see more research in this space.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你看到了这个领域有更多的研究。

sentences.en: And after more than 100 years of making anti-venom with the horses and the snakes,
sentences.zh: 在用马和蛇制造抗毒血清100多年后，

sentences.en: now there's all these new ideas on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 现在地平线上出现了所有这些新想法。

sentences.en: And Jose Maria says that this has all been huge.
sentences.zh: 何塞·玛丽亚说这一切意义重大。

sentences.en: Things have really changed.
sentences.zh: 情况真的改变了。

sentences.en: The world in general is paying much more attention to this disease.
sentences.zh: 整个世界都在更加关注这种疾病。

sentences.en: And it's really exciting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: So now that snakebites have gotten the amount of attention they deserve,
sentences.zh: 既然蛇咬伤已经得到了它们应有的关注，

sentences.en: where are we with the universal anti-venom?
sentences.zh: 通用抗毒血清的进展如何了？

sentences.en: We're starting to see some really exciting things in the science.
sentences.zh: 我们开始在科学上看到一些非常令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: So one of them is that at the same time as snakebites have gotten all this extra attention,
sentences.zh: 其中之一是，在蛇咬伤得到所有这些额外关注的同时，

sentences.en: science has also developed these better tools to be able to look inside venom and analyze those toxins.
sentences.zh: 科学也开发出了更好的工具，能够深入毒液内部并分析那些毒素。

sentences.en: And what we're realizing is that even though there are thousands of toxins doing slightly different things,
sentences.zh: 我们意识到，尽管有成千上万种毒素在做着略有不同的事情，

sentences.en: you can actually group them together into families of toxins and then try and tackle those families.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以将它们归类为毒素家族，然后尝试攻克这些家族。

sentences.en: And it's a much easier target.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更容易的目标。

sentences.en: You can think about it like this.
sentences.zh: 你可以这样想。

sentences.en: Are you a basketball fan?
sentences.zh: 你是篮球迷吗？

sentences.en: Not especially, but continue on.
sentences.zh: 不算特别迷，但请继续。

sentences.en: Excellent.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Huge basketball fan in the corner here.
sentences.zh: 角落里有一位超级篮球迷。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So this is kind of how I've been thinking about the way that they're tackling this universal anti-venom problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是我一直在思考他们解决通用抗毒血清问题的方式。

sentences.en: If, say, you're in the NBA and you've got to play against hundreds of players in the league,
sentences.zh: 如果，比如说，你在NBA，你必须和联盟里的数百名球员比赛，

sentences.en: one way to do that would be to try and figure out the defense of all the individual players.
sentences.zh: 一种方法是试图找出所有个人球员的防守方式。

sentences.en: You know, Curry, LeBron, and even all the middle-level players and all the ones on the bench,
sentences.zh: 你知道，库里、勒布朗，甚至所有中等水平的球员和替补席上的所有人，

sentences.en: like even Beaubon, you've got to work out what's going on with him.
sentences.zh: 比如连别利察，你都得搞清楚他是什么情况。

sentences.en: Well, of course.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, I think about Beaubon all the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我一直都在想别利察。

sentences.en: But I guess contextually I'm to assume that Beaubon is not exactly a LeBron or a Curry.
sentences.zh: 但我猜从语境上讲，我应该假设别利察并不完全是勒布朗或库里那样的球员。

sentences.en: No, but he's doing his beSt.
sentences.zh: 不，但他正在尽他最大的努力。

sentences.en: Okay, great.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: So you've got to work out each player's individual tricks.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须搞清楚每个球员个人的招数。

sentences.en: Instead, what we're doing now is we're just looking at what the big dangerous players are doing
sentences.zh: 相反，我们现在做的是只看那些危险的大牌球员在做什么，

sentences.en: and grouping them together and then working out a defense against them.
sentences.zh: 把他们归类在一起，然后制定针对他们的防守策略。

sentences.en: So just focusing on Steph Curry and all the Curry copycats out there.
sentences.zh: 所以只专注于斯蒂芬·库里和所有像库里那样的模仿者。

sentences.en: Okay, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 好的，这说得通。

sentences.en: So if you know that the toxin hits a lot of three-pointers,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你知道这种毒素投中了很多三分球，

sentences.en: you're basically like making a medicine to deal with that particular attack.
sentences.zh: 你基本上就像是在制造一种药物来应对那种特定的攻击。

sentences.en: It's the anti-three-pointer medicine.
sentences.zh: 这就是“反三分球”药物。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And so has this approach been working so far?
sentences.zh: 那么这种方法到目前为止有效吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's been going well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，进展顺利。

sentences.en: So for example, there's this big family of enzymes that are swimming inside venom.
sentences.zh: 例如，毒液中游动着一个巨大的酶家族。

sentences.en: And what they do is damage blood vessels.
sentences.zh: 它们的作用是破坏血管。

sentences.en: And they're called metalloproteinases.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为金属蛋白酶。

sentences.en: And they're found in vipers all around the world.
sentences.zh: 它们存在于世界各地的蝰蛇体内。

sentences.en: And so scientists have now been searching for a way to basically stop metalloproteinases from working.
sentences.zh: 因此，科学家们现在一直在寻找一种从根本上阻止金属蛋白酶发挥作用的方法。

sentences.en: This is one of those scientists.
sentences.zh: 这位就是其中一位科学家。

sentences.en: Go on, introduce yourself.
sentences.zh: 来吧，自我介绍一下。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I'm Laura Alblescu.
sentences.zh: 好的，我是劳拉·阿尔布莱斯库。

sentences.en: I work at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine.
sentences.zh: 我在利物浦热带医学院工作。

sentences.en: And scientists like Laura are trying to figure out how to protect us against that big family of nasty enzymes.
sentences.zh: 像劳拉这样的科学家正试图找出如何保护我们免受这一大类有害酶的侵害。

sentences.en: And to do that, she's been thinking, well, what do the enzymes need to survive?
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，她一直在思考，这些酶生存需要什么呢？

sentences.en: And they've discovered that one of the things these enzymes need is zinc.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这些酶需要的物质之一是锌。

sentences.en: And Laura says there's actually already a drug on the market that messes with zinc.
sentences.zh: 劳拉说，市场上其实已经有一种药物可以干扰锌的作用。

sentences.en: So Laura and her team took this drug and then combined it with another drug.
sentences.zh: 于是，劳拉和她的团队采用了这种药物，并将其与另一种药物结合使用。

sentences.en: And then they enlisted some heroic little white mice
sentences.zh: 接着，他们找来了一些英勇的小白鼠，

sentences.en: and injected them with some snake venom from some of the most dangerous snakes in the world.
sentences.zh: 并给它们注射了世界上最危险的一些蛇的毒液。

sentences.en: We are looking at vipers from Africa, from India, from Central America.
sentences.zh: 我们观察的是来自非洲、印度和中美洲的蝰蛇。

sentences.en: They waited a bit to let the venom set in, then gave them the concoction, the two drugs.
sentences.zh: 他们等了一会儿让毒液发作，然后给它们服用了那种混合药物。

sentences.en: Now, if this didn't work, most likely...
sentences.zh: 如果这不起作用，很可能……

sentences.en: These mice would all die within a four-hour window.
sentences.zh: 这些小白鼠都会在四小时内死亡。

sentences.en: But instead, the team saw something different.
sentences.zh: 但团队却看到了不同的结果。

sentences.en: The mice started moving around, sniffing.
sentences.zh: 小白鼠开始四处走动、嗅探。

sentences.en: They seemed to be recovering.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎正在康复。

sentences.en: These animals are still alive and look healthy.
sentences.zh: 这些动物仍然活着，看起来很健康。

sentences.en: And how are you feeling?
sentences.zh: 你感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was feeling great.
sentences.zh: 是的，我感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: I didn't expect it to work so well against venoms that are so different from each other.
sentences.zh: 我没想到它对这些截然不同的毒液竟然如此有效。

sentences.en: Yeah, to work for a Fertilance from Central America and then an Asian, you had saw-scaled viper.
sentences.zh: 是啊，能对付中美洲的矛头蝮，还有亚洲的锯鳞蝰，这太厉害了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: How big is that in the world of anti-venom?
sentences.zh: 这在抗毒血清领域有多大的意义？

sentences.en: This is amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: It's really great.
sentences.zh: 真的很棒。

sentences.en: It's really important.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要。

sentences.en: So there you have it.
sentences.zh: 所以，情况就是这样。

sentences.en: After 100 years of needing to inject horses with all these different kinds of venom, Laura's drug has worked.
sentences.zh: 在经历了100年需要给马注射各种不同毒液的日子后，劳拉的药物奏效了。

sentences.en: We did it!
sentences.zh: 我们成功了！

sentences.en: Roman!
sentences.zh: 罗曼！

sentences.en: Well, I have a feeling that we did not do it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有种感觉，我们并没有成功。

sentences.en: That's not how science works.
sentences.zh: 科学不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: One clinical test doesn't do it.
sentences.zh: 一次临床测试说明不了什么。

sentences.en: No, and actually, one of the mice did die 18 hours later.
sentences.zh: 不，而且实际上，其中一只小白鼠在18小时后还是死了。

sentences.en: But, but, but, but, this tactic is actually showing so much promise that there's already a clinical trial in humans underway that's focusing on another drug that messes with zinc.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是，但是，这种策略确实展现出了巨大的前景，目前已经有一项针对人类的临床试验正在进行中，重点研究的是另一种干扰锌的药物。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 那太好了。

sentences.en: And this is a completely different approach.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一种完全不同的方法。

sentences.en: I mean, using drugs rather than using antibodies from another animal is like, it's completely novel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，使用药物而不是使用来自其他动物的抗体，这完全是全新的。

sentences.en: No, exactly.
sentences.zh: 不，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, it's novel in the world of snake bites, but it's what we do for basically every other disease out there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在蛇咬伤领域它是新颖的，但这正是我们处理几乎所有其他疾病的方法。

sentences.en: And, and, you know, the anti-venom that we have now, it does work when you can get it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们现在拥有的抗毒血清，只要能弄到，确实有效。

sentences.en: And so scientists are thinking that maybe in the shortish term, we might have these new and exciting treatments that kind of work alongside the anti-venom from the horses.
sentences.zh: 所以科学家们认为，也许在短期内，我们可能会有这些令人兴奋的新疗法，与马血清抗毒素协同工作。

sentences.en: It's funny because like, you know, we've spent a year with COVID-19 and we saw a series of vaccines go from design to trial to approval in under a year.
sentences.zh: 很有趣，因为你知道，我们经历了一年的新冠疫情，我们看到一系列疫苗在不到一年的时间里从设计到试验再到获批。

sentences.en: And that's not how science normally works ever.
sentences.zh: 而科学通常从来不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: Usually it's a process where you try things, lots of mice die.
sentences.zh: 通常这是一个尝试的过程，会有很多小白鼠死亡。

sentences.en: And after years of experiments, I mean, maybe we have a small breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 经过多年的实验，也许我们能取得一点小突破。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the COVID-19 story, it could tell us two things and time will tell.
sentences.zh: 我认为新冠疫情的故事可以告诉我们两件事，时间会证明一切。

sentences.en: Like, perhaps this virus was actually surprisingly easy to make a vaccine for.
sentences.zh: 也许这种病毒实际上出奇地容易研制出疫苗。

sentences.en: And we were kind of lucky and a nastier virus could have come around that we couldn't have had a vaccine for.
sentences.zh: 我们有点幸运，如果出现一种更糟糕的病毒，我们可能就无法研制出疫苗了。

sentences.en: But maybe the other lesson here is that if scientists get bucket loads of money and basically you encourage nerds from all around the world to tackle a problem,
sentences.zh: 但也许另一个教训是，如果科学家们得到大量的资金，并且你鼓励全世界的书呆子们去攻克一个难题，

sentences.en: that they could solve it very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们就能很快解决它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's like a Manhattan Project or, you know, sending a person to the moon.
sentences.zh: 这就像曼哈顿计划，或者说把人送上月球一样。

sentences.en: You know, it's just like if you put enough money and will behind it, you can make it happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，只要投入足够的资金和意志，你就能让它实现。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so maybe that will happen with snake anti-venom too, if enough scientists and there's enough excitement around this area.
sentences.zh: 所以也许蛇类抗毒血清也会发生同样的情况，如果有足够的科学家和足够多的关注度。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I have one more question before we go.
sentences.zh: 在我们结束之前，我还有一个问题。

sentences.en: Like, what happened to Pete?
sentences.zh: 皮特后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: You know, he got bit by this snake.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他被那条蛇咬了。

sentences.en: He nearly died.
sentences.zh: 他差点死了。

sentences.en: Is he still traipsing around as this conservationist GI Joe?
sentences.zh: 他还在像个环保主义者的特种部队士兵一样四处奔波吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's no change in Pete whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 皮特一点都没变。

sentences.en: He is still in Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 他还在哥斯达黎加。

sentences.en: He's going to be patrolling the jungle soon.
sentences.zh: 他很快就要去丛林巡逻了。

sentences.en: And he said his leg is doing all right.
sentences.zh: 他说他的腿恢复得不错。

sentences.en: In the meantime, he actually still holds a little place in his heart for the snake that got him.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他心里其实还给咬他的那条蛇留了一点位置。

sentences.en: I'm happy that guy's still alive and up there.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴那家伙还活着，还在那里。

sentences.en: So you don't hold a grudge against the snakey?
sentences.zh: 所以你对那条蛇没有怨恨？

sentences.en: No, I don't hold a grudge against the snake.
sentences.zh: 不，我不怨恨那条蛇。

sentences.en: He was just doing snake things.
sentences.zh: 它只是在做蛇该做的事。

sentences.en: Pete has a good attitude.
sentences.zh: 皮特的心态很好。

sentences.en: Thank you, Wendy.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，温迪。

sentences.en: Thanks, Raymond.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，雷蒙德。

sentences.en: More strange, fascinating snake content with Wendy Zuckerman after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后，温迪·扎克曼将带来更多关于蛇的奇妙内容。

sentences.en: So I'm back with Wendy Zuckerman from Science vs. Wendy.
sentences.zh: 我又回到了《科学对决》节目，我是温迪·扎克曼。

sentences.en: Let us talk more about snakes.
sentences.zh: 让我们多聊聊蛇吧。

sentences.en: Yes, please.
sentences.zh: 好的，请继续。

sentences.en: So as I've been researching this episode, I realized there were all these things about snakes that I had never thought about before.
sentences.zh: 在研究这一集时，我意识到关于蛇有太多我以前从未想过的事情。

sentences.en: Like, they're quite beautiful.
sentences.zh: 比如，它们其实很漂亮。

sentences.en: They have all these different colors on their scales.
sentences.zh: 它们的鳞片上有各种不同的颜色。

sentences.en: And I also realized how little science knows about some what I would have thought were pretty basic snake things.
sentences.zh: 我也意识到，科学对于一些我原以为很基础的蛇类知识了解得有多么少。

sentences.en: Like, for example?
sentences.zh: 比如呢？

sentences.en: Like, scientists still aren't sure if snakes can hear.
sentences.zh: 比如，科学家们仍然不确定蛇是否能听见声音。

sentences.en: Like, hear it all?
sentences.zh: 是完全听不见吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: So Dr. Christina Zdenik, who we heard from in the first half of the show, she's like, you know, we know snakes can feel vibrations.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目上半部分听到的克里斯蒂娜·兹德尼克博士说，我们知道蛇能感觉到振动。

sentences.en: That's what we're taught.
sentences.zh: 这是我们被教导的知识。

sentences.en: I don't know if – I actually don't know if you're taught this in a – but every Australian knows that if you see a snake, you've got to, like, stamp your feet.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否在……但我知道每个澳大利亚人都知道，如果你看到一条蛇，你必须跺脚。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, to try and get them to feel –
sentences.zh: 你知道，试图让它们感觉到——

sentences.en: Okay, so we know snakes can feel vibrations, but we didn't know whether they could hear sounds through the air.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以我们知道蛇能感觉到振动，但我们不知道它们是否能通过空气听到声音。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And a big reason for that is that they don't have external ears.
sentences.zh: 一个主要原因是它们没有外耳。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which ever since she told me that, I just can't stop imagining a snake with external ears.
sentences.zh: 自从她告诉我这一点后，我就无法停止想象一条长着外耳的蛇。

sentences.en: With ears.
sentences.zh: 长着耳朵。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, that is the only way we'd really know is if they had big old ears.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们真正知道的唯一方法就是如果它们有大耳朵。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Not on their side of their heads.
sentences.zh: 不是长在头两侧的那种。

sentences.en: And so because they don't have this – you know, for a long time, some scientists were like, well, we just don't think they can hear.
sentences.zh: 因为它们没有这个——你知道，很长一段时间里，一些科学家认为，嗯，我们只是觉得它们听不见。

sentences.en: Yeah, and then Christina heard this kind of amazing story from one of her colleagues.
sentences.zh: 是的，然后克里斯蒂娜从她的一位同事那里听到了一个惊人的故事。

sentences.en: Damien Canduso.
sentences.zh: 达米安·坎杜索。

sentences.en: And I want to tell you, I mean, in some ways it's like I can't – I can't imagine a more stereotypical Australian story.
sentences.zh: 我想告诉你，在某些方面，我无法想象还有比这更典型的澳大利亚故事了。

sentences.en: So I am nervous to bring this to more Americans, but –
sentences.zh: 所以我很紧张，不知道该不该向更多的美国人讲述这个，但是——

sentences.en: That you're in a safe space here.
sentences.zh: 在这里你是安全的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So this guy, he sometimes makes the sound effects for films, and he noticed that while he was working on what he called low-end frequencies,
sentences.zh: 这个家伙有时会为电影制作音效，他注意到当他在处理所谓的低频声音时，

sentences.en: so think like bombs exploding, you know, that like – and like earthquakes where you hear those tremors in a cinema.
sentences.zh: 比如炸弹爆炸，你知道，还有地震，你在电影院里听到的那种震动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so while he was creating those sounds, he would notice that brown snakes would start slithering next to his house from seemingly nowhere.
sentences.zh: 当他制作这些声音时，他注意到棕蛇会从不知何处滑到他房子旁边。

sentences.en: He didn't know why.
sentences.zh: 他不知道为什么。

sentences.en: It could have been a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个巧合。

sentences.en: It could have been that they were feeling vibrations, or maybe because they really could hear the sound waves through the air.
sentences.zh: 可能是它们感觉到了振动，或者是因为它们真的能通过空气听到声波。

sentences.en: And so he ends up telling this story to Christina, and Christina was like, yeah, you know, there are a few studies suggesting like maybe snakes can hear.
sentences.zh: 他最终把这个故事告诉了克里斯蒂娜，克里斯蒂娜说，是的，有一些研究表明蛇可能确实能听见。

sentences.en: You know, still this huge debate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这仍然是一个巨大的争论。

sentences.en: And so just this year, they teamed up and decided to test it.
sentences.zh: 所以就在今年，他们联手决定进行测试。

sentences.en: We've got a soundproof room, and we've got 19 captive snakes.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个隔音室，还有19条圈养的蛇。

sentences.en: What her team does is they take the snake out of its holding container, which is essentially like a rubbish bin with some holes in the lid.
sentences.zh: 她的团队把蛇从容器里拿出来，那基本上就是一个带孔盖子的垃圾桶。

sentences.en: Grabbing the snake with a hook.
sentences.zh: 用钩子抓住蛇。

sentences.en: And then with his hand when it's safe.
sentences.zh: 安全的时候再用手抓。

sentences.en: And then they put the snake into this soundproof room.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把蛇放进这个隔音室。

sentences.en: We've got a half wall, which we've just secured the door for, for security.
sentences.zh: 我们有一堵半墙，为了安全起见，我们刚刚锁好了门。

sentences.en: Christina sent me a photo.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜给我发了一张照片。

sentences.en: It's literally fancier than the Gimlet Studios and definitely more secure.
sentences.zh: 它确实比Gimlet工作室更高级，而且绝对更安全。

sentences.en: And then they give the snake some time to settle.
sentences.zh: 然后他们让蛇适应一下环境。

sentences.en: So then they play some sounds through this very special setup they have that's basically designed so that the sounds come through the air and they don't make vibrations on the floor.
sentences.zh: 接着他们通过一种非常特殊的装置播放声音，这种装置的设计初衷是让声音通过空气传播，而不会在地面上产生振动。

sentences.en: I see, right.
sentences.zh: 我明白了，对。

sentences.en: And then she's basically recording the snake's behavior.
sentences.zh: 然后她基本上是在记录蛇的行为。

sentences.en: So what did they find?
sentences.zh: 那么他们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Do snakes actually hear the sound?
sentences.zh: 蛇真的能听到声音吗？

sentences.en: Okay, she's still analyzing the data, but here's what she told me about it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，她还在分析数据，但这是她告诉我的情况。

sentences.en: There's some very interesting behaviors.
sentences.zh: 有一些非常有趣的行为。

sentences.en: I think it will be clear, at least with some of the individuals, that they're absolutely going to be aware of the sound.
sentences.zh: 我认为至少对于某些个体来说，很明显它们绝对能察觉到声音。

sentences.en: What I think is pretty cool with what Christina is starting to see is that the behaviors she's seeing is really dependent on the individual snake.
sentences.zh: 我认为克里斯蒂娜开始观察到的现象很酷，那就是她看到的行为确实取决于蛇的个体差异。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And so here's what she said about that.
sentences.zh: 以下是她对此的看法。

sentences.en: How they respond, I think, it seems to be based on the individual personality,
sentences.zh: 我认为它们的反应似乎是基于个体性格，

sentences.en: whether they're a type of a timid snake or whether they're sort of more defensive and willing to give more defensive behaviors.
sentences.zh: 无论它们是胆小的蛇，还是更具防御性、愿意表现出更多防御行为的蛇。

sentences.en: And by that, a snake would be dropping their lower jaw to show their fangs or hissing.
sentences.zh: 所谓防御行为，就是蛇会张开下颚露出毒牙，或者发出嘶嘶声。

sentences.en: Had you thought about snakes as having personalities?
sentences.zh: 你有没有想过蛇也有个性？

sentences.en: Yes, we see it all the time.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们经常见到这种情况。

sentences.en: And so my husband and I, we have 24 snakes as pets.
sentences.zh: 我和我丈夫养了24条蛇作为宠物。

sentences.en: And so we see it on a very intimate level.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对此有着非常深刻的了解。

sentences.en: One snake doesn't like to be touched.
sentences.zh: 有的蛇不喜欢被触碰。

sentences.en: Another one could care less.
sentences.zh: 有的则完全不在乎。

sentences.en: One basically like falls asleep in your hands.
sentences.zh: 有的在你手里基本就睡着了。

sentences.en: He's like this old man.
sentences.zh: 它就像个老人家一样。

sentences.en: He's literally 21 years old.
sentences.zh: 他才21岁。

sentences.en: He's like, you know, 2.2 meter coast of Taipan.
sentences.zh: 他就像是，你知道的，2.2米长的海岸太攀蛇。

sentences.en: Like they're very sort of predictable in their personalities.
sentences.zh: 就像它们的性格非常容易预测一样。

sentences.en: And so to take this back to the experiment, so in the tape where we were hearing about the experiment,
sentences.zh: 回到刚才的实验，在录音带里我们听到了关于实验的内容，

sentences.en: Christina's describing the snake that's hissing and getting all pissy at the sound.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜描述了那条听到声音后发出嘶嘶声并变得非常暴躁的蛇。

sentences.en: That's a coastal Taipan.
sentences.zh: 那是一条海岸太攀蛇。

sentences.en: But it's not this sleepy guy that she's talking about here.
sentences.zh: 但它并不是她在这里提到的那个昏昏欲睡的家伙。

sentences.en: That sleepy guy was also in the experiment and she said that he basically fell asleep when he heard the sounds.
sentences.zh: 那个昏昏欲睡的家伙也参与了实验，她说它在听到声音时基本上就睡着了。

sentences.en: So it's like this perfect example of how she's seeing these different reactions.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一个完美的例子，展示了她是如何观察到这些不同反应的。

sentences.en: By the way, just to get a sense of how big that sleepy snake is, she said 2.2 meters.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，为了让你了解那条贪睡的蛇有多大，她说有2.2米长。

sentences.en: It's about the same height as Bobon, the basketball player.
sentences.zh: 这差不多和篮球运动员博班的身高一样。

sentences.en: It all comes back to Bobon.
sentences.zh: 一切又回到了博班身上。

sentences.en: That's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Did you ever think of snakes as having personalities?
sentences.zh: 你有没有想过蛇也有个性？

sentences.en: I mean, I had a snake and I didn't have a lot of exposure.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我养过一条蛇，但我接触得不多。

sentences.en: That one seemed to have a personality.
sentences.zh: 那条蛇看起来确实有个性。

sentences.en: It was named Chewbacca.
sentences.zh: 它叫丘巴卡。

sentences.en: It was a corn snake.
sentences.zh: 那是一条玉米锦蛇。

sentences.en: But like I didn't have a lot of other snakes to compare it to.
sentences.zh: 但我没有太多其他的蛇可以用来做比较。

sentences.en: So it had personality, but I didn't realize how, you know, maybe different it was from other corn snakes.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实有个性，但我没意识到它和其他玉米锦蛇相比，可能有多么不同。

sentences.en: But, you know, Chewie was a great snake and would escape on occasion and then show up four days later, like right next to the cage.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道，丘伊是一条很棒的蛇，偶尔会溜走，然后四天后又出现，就像出现在笼子旁边一样。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，哇。

sentences.en: Like a cat.
sentences.zh: 就像猫一样。

sentences.en: Like cats do that.
sentences.zh: 猫确实会那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So it doesn't surprise me that they have some personality.
sentences.zh: 所以它们有自己的个性，我一点也不觉得奇怪。

sentences.en: The fact that one would, you know, get really exercised upon watching a Christopher Nolan movie, another one would be completely nonplussed by it.
sentences.zh: 事实就是，有的猫在看克里斯托弗·诺兰的电影时会变得非常兴奋，而有的猫则对此完全无动于衷。

sentences.en: It's new to me, though.
sentences.zh: 不过这对我来说还是新鲜事。

sentences.en: That's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: And new to science, I think.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这对科学界来说也是新鲜事。

sentences.en: I like it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
